lens: candidate identity, evidence provenance, uncertainty, human authorization, receipt and readback integrity, privacy lifecycle, sensitive inference boundaries, and evaluator reliability

findings.observation: Confirmed defect: deleting a governed source removes the source text but does not remove source-derived Proposal narrative. The frozen post-delete readback still returns the Proposal summary, item before/proposed values, reason, and effect summary. The deletion implementation only supersedes open pursuit_proposals; it does not redact pursuit_proposals.summary or pursuit_proposal_items narrative/value fields, while deletion_lineage records both Proposal entities as content_removed and the receipt reports derivatives_deleted. This contradicts the frozen architecture and delivery claim that source deletion reaches every registered derivative.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-final-panel-retest-02/evidence/pursuit-evidence/pursuit-evidence-integrity-runtime.json:484-582 returns summary 'The first source may support a milestone change.' and reason 'The candidate described a scheduling step.' after deletion, with lineage_types including pursuit_proposal and pursuit_proposal_item at 590-602; apps/backend/src/modules/captures.ts:825-857 registers those entities, 1143-1167 only changes open Proposal status, and 1613-1629 labels every non-effect entity content_removed; apps/backend/src/modules/pursuitProposals.ts:303-338 maps the retained fields back to API responses; docs/architecture.md:267 and docs/delivery.md:30-31 promise derivative propagation. All cited files and the runtime evidence matched the frozen artifact hashes.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can receive a successful deletion receipt while sensitive candidate-derived wording remains stored and retrievable. That makes the disclosed deletion control materially false and can preserve precisely the content the person or recruiter intended to remove.
findings.recommendation: Separate minimal, purpose-justified structured decision history from source-derived narrative. On source deletion, redact Proposal summary, reason, effect summary, decision reason, and any free-form or copied values that can restate the source; retain only the minimum identifiers, enum/value transition where justified, actor, time, and Receipt needed for audit. Make each lineage disposition describe the actual retained or removed state rather than labeling retained content content_removed.
findings.verification: Seed unique canaries into source text and every Proposal/free-form derivative, apply and leave-open variants, then delete the source. Prove the canaries are absent from all Proposal APIs, database columns, idempotency payloads, audit/event payloads, caches, exports, backups, and vendor stores; prove the surviving milestone value shows authority unavailable with actor/time/Proposal/Receipt only; and prove derivatives_deleted and lineage dispositions match the actual field-level result.

findings.criterion: Owner outcome write integrity and response-loss recovery
findings.observation: Credible risk: the backend correctly scopes action completion to the current canonical owner and uses revision checks plus an idempotency key, but the iOS owner-outcome path creates a fresh operation UUID for each invocation and persists no pending operation or unknown-locked state. It reloads canonical state only after a successful response. If the server commits and the response is lost, the UI can report failure; a user retry creates a new idempotency key and meets a terminal action instead of reconciling the committed operation. The frozen response-loss proof covers Proposal review, not owner action completion.
findings.evidence: apps/ios/Sources/Features/PursuitWorkspaceStore.swift:90-108 defaults operationID to UUID(), calls the service, and only then reloads; apps/ios/Sources/Services/PursuitWorkspaceClient.swift:122-165 derives the idempotency key from that transient UUID and provides no operation readback path. apps/backend/src/modules/pursuits.ts:1121-1133 proves same-key replay, 1178-1198 proves owner/revision/terminal guards, and 1211-1257 proves one internal outcome with zero external effects. docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-final-panel-retest-02/evidence/pursuit-domain/pursuit-domain-runtime.json proves happy-path and same-key replay, while the frozen response-loss artifacts and ios-full-suite-runtime.json are Proposal-review scenarios rather than action-completion scenarios.
findings.user_impact: After an ambiguous network failure, the recruiter may be told an outcome was not recorded even though it is canonical, then be unable to tell whether retry is safe. This is a truthfulness and recovery failure even though the backend prevents a duplicate state transition.
findings.recommendation: Persist the action-completion operation ID before submission, enter an explicit unknown-locked state on any ambiguous result, disable resubmission, and reconcile by operation ID plus canonical action readback. Validate receipt operation ID, actor/owner, operation kind, status, exact changed fields, before/after revisions, and zero external effects before presenting success.
findings.verification: Drop the response after backend commit on Simulator and real device, terminate and relaunch, and repeat at least ten times. Every run must show unknown rather than failure/success before readback, issue exactly one completion POST and one canonical Receipt, reconcile with the original operation ID, and show the exact owner-entered outcome without a second mutation.

findings.observation: Credible risk: current milestone authority is inferred by finding the latest confirmed or edited Proposal item whose decided value equals the current milestone. It is not bound to the mutation that most recently established that value. A direct user revision can move A to B via a Proposal, then B to C directly, then C back to B directly; the read path can attach the old Proposal's evidence, confirmer, time, and Receipt to the new user-authored B state.
findings.evidence: apps/backend/src/modules/pursuits.ts:482-497 filters Proposal items by decided_value equal to pursuits.milestone and orders only Proposal decision time; it does not compare the latest direct Pursuit mutation or a current-authority pointer. The frozen pursuit-evidence runtime proves deletion-aware authority for the simple applied-Proposal case but contains no Proposal-to-direct-revision-to-same-value sequence.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can see a current milestone presented as evidence-backed by an older candidate source even though the latest change was a separate recruiter-authored action, blurring evidence, confirmed state, and human interpretation.
findings.recommendation: Persist an explicit authority record or immutable current-mutation pointer on every milestone write. Read authority from that exact mutation, not from value equality; direct edits must replace the current authority with user-authored provenance even when they restore an earlier value.
findings.verification: Apply evidence-backed A to B, directly revise B to C, directly revise C to B, and read the Pursuit before and after deleting the old source. The B milestone must remain attributed to the final direct editor and mutation Receipt, never to the older Proposal; add concurrent and replay variants.

strengths: The prior same-name identity failure is resolved in the frozen synthetic path: selection exposes stable Person, Pursuit, role, and relationship-context clues; no automatic choice is made when two scopes exist; the selected Person/context survives relaunch; and the canonical receipt repeats the exact bound identifiers. ios-full-suite-runtime.json reports the same-name test passing and same-name-binding-receipt.png visibly distinguishes the selected Alex Chen.

Proposal review no longer presents success from a mismatched or malformed Receipt: the pending operation ID is persisted, ambiguous results become unknown-locked, canonical operation readback is required, and operation/proposal/workspace/revision/outcome/changed-field/external-effect checks are covered by the frozen full suite and pursuit-proposal runtime.

The applied-milestone read surface now keeps the confirmed value while visibly degrading evidence authority to unavailable after source deletion and preserving confirmer, time, Proposal, and Receipt. This fixes the authority-status portion of the prior deletion problem, independently of the remaining narrative-retention veto.

Owner outcome completion has strong server-side boundaries: exact account, Pursuit, action, owner, and revisions are checked; the observed outcome is required; same-key replay returns the same Receipt; and external effects remain empty. The frozen canonical-action-outcome screenshots show the exact outcome and Receipt rather than an external-send claim.

The Agent control plane is proposal-only in the frozen deterministic evidence: its manifest is limited to read_pursuit, read_evidence, stage_pursuit_proposal, and record_no_action; active reviewed attributed evidence and workspace scope are enforced; 30 deterministic trials report zero external effects; and candidate scoring or sensitive inference is outside the contract.

All 181 declared source files, 13 runtime evidence files, and 9 screenshots matched the SHA-256 hashes in artifact TS-V1-FINAL-20260824-02; the recomputed source aggregate matched 3ac0e815c210cafd6358d9e8cad1da6f96f91b92fd0449fb1ed3180cd383b90f.
missing_evidence: No manual VoiceOver traversal of the complete capture, same-name selection, Proposal review, outcome, Receipt, retry, deletion, and recovery journey; automated accessibility labels and AX5 screenshots are not a substitute.
No physical-device proof for Action Button, microphone and system capture behavior, interruption, foreground enforcement, revoke/delete, or iOS Data Protection while locked.

The frozen live-Claude artifact is not_run_missing_credentials: there are zero of the required five credentialed trials, no pinned observed model, and no live-provider malformed/timeout/retry reconciliation proof.

No production proof for authentication/session expiry, real cross-tenant isolation, retention expiry, deletion through backups/caches/analytics/exports/vendors, regional processing, provider reconciliation, or credentialed external-write integrations; production and real credentials were intentionally excluded.
No field or design-partner evidence with authorized real recruiter workflows, no candidate-side trust/consent research, and no real candidate data; the artifact is synthetic-only.
No frozen response-loss, relaunch, malformed-Receipt, or actor/operation-kind mismatch test for the owner action-outcome client path.
No canary-based proof that source-derived Proposal narrative is removed from every raw and derived store after source deletion; the frozen runtime instead confirms retention in the API readback.
No adversarial sequence proving milestone authority follows the latest direct mutation when a later user edit restores an older evidence-backed value.
No human gold set, blinded evaluator calibration, order-swap stability, counterexample suite, or drift monitoring for the evaluator itself.
No measured OCR replay quality across bounding boxes, languages, low-confidence text, speaker ambiguity, and correction rates on an authorized corpus.
vetoes: Active privacy veto: source deletion is reported as complete and Proposal/Proposal-item lineage is labeled content_removed while source-derived Proposal summary, reason, effect, and value content remains stored and retrievable.
open_questions: Which exact Proposal and Proposal-item fields are policy-approved to survive source deletion, for what retention period and purpose, and why are retained rows currently recorded as content_removed?
What canonical operation endpoint and persisted client state will reconcile an owner action outcome after response loss without a new idempotency key?
Will every direct milestone edit write an explicit authority mutation so that current provenance never depends on value equality with historical Proposals?
What are the production retention, backup purge, export, vendor deletion, regional processing, and incident-monitoring commitments for candidate evidence and its derivatives?
